text: Mr Zhulkarnain also asked why the updated definition is adapted from the definition of abuse in the Vulnerable Adults Act 2018 (VAA).

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Both this Act and the Women's Charter are regimes that aim to protect those experiencing abuse.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The profiles of persons they protect are different.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, the VAA protects those who are incapable of protecting themselves due to mental or physical infirmity, disability or incapacity and, therefore, the interventions are different.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, the abuse they target is the same.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Hence, we have aligned the definitions of abuse in these two regimes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will help promote a common understanding of abusive behaviour amongst the public, professionals in the social service sector, the Courts and lawyers, and facilitate better detection and identification of acts of abuse.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Hany Soh asked whether Protectors would be able to make applications for PPOs on behalf of survivors, such as those below 18, who are willing but unable to apply for them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Chua sought clarification on our rationale for the minimum age of a PPO applicant.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: All survivors are entitled to receive timely legal protection.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Survivors who are aged below 18 may seek assistance from other family members, social service professionals or Protectors, to apply for a PPO on his or her behalf.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They can also be accorded the necessary protection and support under the Children and Young Persons Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng suggested that the Court automatically grants PPOs for the survivor's vulnerable dependants when the survivor himself or herself is granted a PPO by the Court.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is aligned with the current practice and there is a good reason for this.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, an individual may inflict violence only on the spouse and not on the children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: While a PPO application must be made for each family member, and a PPO will be issued if the Court is satisfied that the perpetrator has committed or is likely to commit family violence against each family member and that the protection order is necessary for his or her protection, the Court may give direction for the applications to be heard together and this will help families save time and resources.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Hany Soh asked if there were measures to prevent estranged spouses from abusing the enhanced family violence regime during divorce proceedings.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Access to justice is a fundamental right and all parties must have the avenues to apply for a PPO.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But this is not to say that a person can abuse the Court process and make frivolous or vexatious applications.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I had mentioned earlier, a PPO is only issued when the Court is satisfied that the respondent has committed or is likely to commit family violence against the applicant or other family member(s) concerned and it is necessary for his or her protection or safety.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In addition, if the application is frivolous or vexatious, the Court may order costs to be paid for by the applicant.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In extreme cases, the Court can make Civil Restraint Orders to restrain a person from bringing further applications without the Court's permission.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked that we consider if family violence re-offenders could be identified, to deter re-offending and to protect others from harm.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: He also acknowledged that doing so may lead to the identification of the survivor.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The purpose of prohibiting publication or broadcast of information that is likely to identify family violence survivors is solely to protect survivors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The intent is to encourage survivors to report family violence incidents without the fear of being publicly embarrassed and to spare survivors who do report such incidents from further trauma.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Early this year, I received an email from Mrs N.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: She shared that her ex-husband was being prosecuted for breaching a PPO and her identity was publicly disclosed as it was an open hearing.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As it took her great courage to report the family violence, she was worried that her child's psychological well-being would be negatively impacted since her and her ex-husband's names were made known publicly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This amendment would protect Mrs N and her child's identities as the publication of their identities will be prohibited by law, even in the absence of a gag order.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mrs N would also be able to apply to the Court to remove the publication.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will accord Mrs N and her child the space and privacy to recover and heal from the trauma.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, if the survivor consents to the publication or broadcast of such information that could identify him or her, the Director-General of Social Welfare (DGSW) will regard his or her consent as a highly relevant factor and may decide to grant approval for such publication or broadcast.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the validity of PPOs following the imprisonment of offenders, and arrangements to ensure the survivor's continued protection during and after the perpetrator's imprisonment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Hence, in most cases, PPOs which are issued before the term of imprisonment will continue to remain in force after the perpetrator's imprisonment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Depending on the circumstances of each survivor, social service professionals may conduct safety planning and provide assistance and support if the survivors need legal advice, shelter or financial support.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Hany Soh and Mr Louis Chua asked whether MSF will provide assistance for perpetrators and survivors who are subject to Domestic Exclusion, No Contact or Stay Away Orders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Social service professionals at our Protection Specialist Centres and Family Service Centres will continue to work closely with families, survivors and perpetrators to provide any needed assistance, such as shelter and financial support.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Louis Ng and Ms Sylvia Lim spoke on ensuring sufficient resourcing and support for the persons, such as Protectors, who assist the Director-General to ensure this important work is carried out properly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Protectors, who are authorised by the Director-General to exercise powers under this Bill, are social service professionals who are trained in managing family violence and protection cases and have expertise in trauma-informed care and support.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They are committed to ensuring the well-being and safety of families affected by violence and have a keen awareness of the unique needs and challenges faced by the families they serve.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is physically and emotionally demanding work and we will ensure that our Protectors continue to be provided with the necessary resources, such as sufficient manpower, training and access to up-to-date research, to exercise the new powers in this Bill and tackle family violence effectively.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked about safeguards against the abuse of the Protector's powers and whether there are any avenues to appeal against an Emergency Order.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Emergency Orders issued by Protectors are intended to cover an existing gap.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These Orders will be time-limited, to give the survivors time to apply for a PPO from the Court.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There is also a limit to the number of times an Emergency Order can be made.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I agree with Mr Zhulkarnain's suggestion that there should be greater public awareness that powers to remove survivors will only be exercised as a last resort.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will only be considered in high-risk circumstances, when all other social service interventions have failed, in order to ensure the protection and safety of the survivors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked if the Police would continue to process cases as per usual, if arrestable offences are disclosed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Police would continue to address cases as per usual, if arrestable offences are disclosed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In high-risk family violence situations, the Police will jointly respond with the Domestic Violence Emergency Team, or DVET.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Police will continue to handle cases with law-and-order issues.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The DVET officers will address immediate safety concerns and refer the families to Protection Specialist Centres for follow-up intervention.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng asked for more details on the Electronic Monitoring Order.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Details of the electronic monitoring regime will be worked out further by MSF.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if there are plans to arrange for higher levels of policing as a deterrence measure to complement PPOs and the new Court Orders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If we refer to both the Member's earlier clarification on concerns about abuse of the Electronic Monitoring regime and his current suggestion to have more monitoring and policing as a practical deterrence, I think we need to ask ourselves what is the balance that we ought to strike.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I would say that we need to put the survivor at the heart of what we do.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We want to protect them while ensuring that their privacy is also safeguarded.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Thus, our social service professionals will continue to work closely with the Police, including their Family Violence Community Policing Officers, to identify, respond to and monitor cases involving very high-risk family violence.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MSF will also continue our public education efforts through the Break the Silence campaign to encourage the community to partner us in detecting, identifying and reporting family violence incidents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To those enduring violence at home, you are not alone.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We want to assure you that there are many resources and channels to support and help you.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If you are unsure of what to do or if you need more information, call the 24-hour National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline at 1800-777-0000.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Social service professionals stand ready to assist you.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To those who are struggling with abusive behaviour, there is hope.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With the right support and intervention, change is possible.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: By stepping forward to seek help from social service agencies, you give yourself a chance to break the cycle of violence, as well as pave the way for a brighter, happier future for yourself and your loved ones.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: So, I understand that this is purely in relation to protection of the identity of the survivors, but not the rest of the family members or the perpetrators.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Take, for example, in situations where the matter was referred to Court by the protector without the survivor's consent and in those situations also where the perpetrators are actually suffering from psychiatric conditions that have caused the commissions of violence.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.25 pm.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.06 pm until 3.25 pm.
